answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a hardware-rooted entry gate. A new agent must prove possession of a distinct secure enclave, and the registry pins every enclave root to a fixed trellis of registered device keys. If a second enrollment presents a root already on that trellis, the comparison returns an echo of the earlier entry and the duplicate is refused. Entry is one narrow lotus: one door, one enclave, one identity. Faking a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand physical chips plus a forfeitable bond per seat, so each extra fake carries real capital outlay instead of a free keypair.
